name: Apollo 17’s third stage
intro: This crater was made by the third stage of the last Saturn V to carry astronauts to the Moon. It launched Apollo 17 on 7 December 1972, the only Saturn V launch at night, and was crashed into the Moon on 10 December, the day before the landing. Look up: the see-through rocket stage over the crater shows how it looked a moment before it hit.

hotspots.title: The crater
hotspots.text: The stage made a crater about 31 meters across. LRO has photographed it many times under different lighting.

source.label: LROC (LRO camera team): the Apollo S-IVB craters

hotspots.title: One big engine
hotspots.text: This is the stage’s single J-2 engine. It burned liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen to push the Apollo ships out of Earth orbit and onto the road to the Moon.

hotspots.title: Mostly fuel tank
hotspots.text: Nearly all of the stage is fuel tank: 17.8 meters tall and 6.6 meters across, about as tall as a six-storey building. By the time it reached the Moon its fuel was used up.

hotspots.title: Steering rockets
hotspots.text: The pods on the sides hold the stage’s small steering rockets, which kept it pointing the right way on its long fall to the Moon.

hotspots.title: The stage in space
hotspots.text: Before the crash, the lunar module rode inside the top of this stage. After the crew pulled it out, the empty stage was steered toward the Moon.

photo.alt: A spacecraft seen from above inside a round opening, surrounded by sparkling dots in black space.
photo.caption: The lunar module on top of the S-IVB, seen from the command module; the dots are bits of debris.
photo.licenseEvidence: NASA Image and Video Library item as17-148-22687 (JSC); no third-party credit or copyright notice on the item. NASA: images and video "generally are not subject to copyright in the United States" (https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/).

hotspots.title: The final dive
hotspots.text: It hit at 2.55 km per second, about 55 degrees above the horizon.

source.label: NSSDCA: Apollo impact sites on the Moon

hotspots.title: Scattered pieces
hotspots.text: Scout’s check: nothing survived in one piece. Its fragments lie scattered around the crater.

source.label: LROC (LRO camera team): the Apollo S-IVB craters

funFact: It was the last Saturn V stage ever to hit the Moon.
whyLeft: Its job ended once it had pushed Challenger and the command module America toward the Moon, so it became one last test signal for the seismometers.
repurpose: It shattered into pieces. Its aluminium could be a source of metal for a future Moon base.

source.label: LROC Featured Sites: Apollo 17 S-IVB, 31 m (depth 2-3 m: Plescia et al. 2016)
